user.title: Crestron PAC2M
user.description:
Found on the network: {found}.

Adding the integration does NOT change the processor. It starts passive: it sends nothing and the lights stay unavailable until you choose 'Go stand-alone' under Configure.

reconfigure.title: Crestron processor address
reconfigure.description:
Current address: {current}. Found on the network: {found}.

Only changes the address Home Assistant uses to reach the processor (for example after it got a new IP). Nothing is sent to the processor and the mode stays the same.

error.already_configured: Another entry already uses this processor

init.title: Crestron PAC2M (current mode: {mode})
init.description: Stand-alone: Home Assistant controls the lights and Control4 stops. Control4: the processor is pointed back at Control4 and this integration disables itself.

menu_options.standalone: Go stand-alone (processor points to Home Assistant)
menu_options.control4: Return to Control4 (processor points to Control4, integration disables itself)
menu_options.settings: Settings (address overrides, phone notification, refresh after restart)

standalone.title: Go stand-alone
standalone.description: Points the Crestron at Home Assistant, reboots it (about 2-4 minutes, lights keep their levels and wall keypads keep working), then moves the existing light entity ids to this integration. The old Control4 lights are renamed and disabled. If Home Assistant never comes online the change is undone automatically. Tick 'Preview only' to see the plan without changing anything.

control4.title: Return to Control4
control4.description: Finds the Control4 address (currently: {control4_host}), points the Crestron back at it, reboots it, restores the original Control4 light entity ids and then disables this integration. Tick 'Preview only' to see the plan without changing anything.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description:
The two addresses are only needed if they cannot be found automatically; leave them empty for automatic. The phone notification service gets a short message for every switch and warning (empty = persistent notification only).

Refresh after a Home Assistant restart (experimental, untested on a real processor): in stand-alone mode, when Home Assistant restarts while the processor keeps the session, run Refresh from processor to get the real light levels. Home Assistant cannot control the lights for about 3 minutes meanwhile; wall keypads keep working. Takes effect at the next start.

data.notify_service: Phone notification service (the part after notify.)
data.refresh_after_restart: Refresh from processor after a Home Assistant restart

learn_name.title: Name the keypad button
learn_name.description: Digital join {join} was pressed. It gets its own event entity (press and release) and no longer shows up on the Digital join entity.

buttons.title: Remove keypad buttons
buttons.description: Ticked buttons lose their event entity; their presses go back to the Digital join entity.

progress.switching: Re-pointing the Crestron processor and rebooting it. This takes a few minutes; you can close this window.
progress.learning: Press the keypad button now (waiting {seconds} s). Don't change lights from Home Assistant meanwhile.

abort.not_connected: The processor link is down (or the integration is in Control4 mode); keypad presses can only be learned while the link is up.
abort.learn_timeout: No new keypad press within {seconds} s. Buttons that already have a name are ignored.

go_standalone.name: Go stand-alone
go_standalone.description: Point the processor at Home Assistant and take over the Control4 light entity ids.

return_to_control4.name: Return to Control4
return_to_control4.description: Point the processor back at Control4, restore its entities and disable this integration.

adopt_entity_ids.name: Adopt entity ids
adopt_entity_ids.description: Give the existing Control4 light entity ids to this integration.

release_entity_ids.name: Release entity ids
release_entity_ids.description: Give the light entity ids back to Control4.

refresh_from_processor.name: Refresh from processor
refresh_from_processor.description: Stand-alone only: go silent so the processor drops the session, then reconnect to get a fresh state dump (current light levels) without a reboot. Experimental.

pause_seconds.name: Pause
pause_seconds.description: How long Home Assistant stays silent. The lights cannot be controlled from Home Assistant meanwhile; wall keypads keep working.

address_changed.title: Crestron processor points at an old Home Assistant address

confirm.title: Re-point the Crestron processor
confirm.description:
The processor's IP table (entry {cip_id}) points at {table_ip}, but Home Assistant is now {ha_ip}, so the lights are unavailable.

Submit runs Go stand-alone: it points the processor at {ha_ip} and reboots it (about 2-4 minutes; lights keep their levels and wall keypads keep working). If Home Assistant never comes online the change is undone. To avoid this in future, give Home Assistant a fixed address in your router.

progress.switching: Re-pointing the Crestron processor and rebooting it. This takes a few minutes.

abort.not_loaded: The Crestron PAC2M integration is not loaded.

label_mismatch.title: Crestron light labels do not match the light table
label_mismatch.description:
{summary}

The processor's names for these joins differ from the light table, so a light entity may control a different light. Check the light table (or crestron_pac2m_lights.yaml). This goes away by itself once the labels match.
